extracted.intended_audience: teachers/instructors of public relations writing courses (college-level)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for instructors on setting goals/objectives and systematically evaluating student public-relations writing assignments by focusing on elements common to all such assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: what the writing is to make a public think or do
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the piece has a clear, appropriate objective directed at a public or audience — i.e., what the writing is intended to make readers think or do. Consider alignment of content and call-to-action with stated purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: persuasive strategy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the choice and execution of persuasive techniques (appeals, organization, messaging) used to accomplish the stated purpose. Judge logic, appeal to audience values, and appropriateness of strategy for the target public.

rubrics_metrics.name: medium
rubrics_metrics.description: the appropriate style, format, and presentation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether the style, formatting, and overall presentation fit the chosen medium (e.g., press release, brochure, memo). Evaluate tone, structure, length, and visual/layout choices for medium-appropriateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: the facts, grammar, spelling, and punctuation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check factual correctness, factual sourcing where applicable, and mechanical correctness including grammar, spelling, and punctuation. Errors that harm credibility should lower the evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: creativity
rubrics_metrics.description: originality in approach, strategy, and use of medium
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate originality of concept, approach, and use of the chosen medium. Consider whether the work shows fresh thinking or imaginative ways to reach the audience while still serving the purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: why a piece of writing did or did not work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge overall effectiveness: whether the piece achieved (or plausibly would achieve) its purpose. Provide diagnostic comments explaining strengths and weaknesses and why the work succeeded or failed in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: prewriting form / planning
rubrics_metrics.description: use of a prewriting form to focus work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teachers are encouraged to provide students a prewriting form to clarify objectives, target public, persuasive strategy, and medium before drafting. The form helps students focus and makes evaluation criteria explicit (a sample form is attached in the original document).
